text:
emma: quick q — planning the quant bakeoff next week (FP8/INT8/GPTQ/AWQ). want to lock the calibration / prompt probe strategy. thinking stratified holdouts + negative controls. thoughts?
raj: +1 for stratified. we need coverage across length, domain, and ambiguity. short/long token splits are crucial for AWQ artifacts.
olivia: agree. also add fuzz/typo noise set — quant can amplify brittleness on broken prompts. small set (2-3k) of edgecases is good.
kai: practical constraints: we have ~50k candidate prompts. proposal: sample 30k train-calib, 10k validation (holdout for metrics), 10k probes (edge/neg controls). keep probe sets balanced across domains and include 200 synthetic adversarial prompts.
emma: can we formalize the strata? i propose: length strata (<16, 16-64, 65-256, >256), domain strata (qa, summarization, instruction, dialog, code), ambiguity strata (clear, ambiguous, underspecified). sample proportionally but oversample ambiguous+long by x2.
raj: sounds good. for comparison across quant formats we should also keep deterministic seeds and same prompt order; mention in config.

olivia: + add prompt templates vs. raw prompts as separate axis. templated prompts interact with instruction tuning differently when quantized.
kai: noted. also include a small set of golden references for semantic evals (human-annotated). we should reserve ~1k examples for human spot-checks post-bakeoff.
emma: drafting sampling config now — will push to repo. short snippet for review:```yaml
seed: 42
sample_sizes:
  calib: 30000
  validation: 10000
  probes: 10000
strata:
  length_bins: [16,64,256]
  domains: [qa,summary,instruct,dialog,code]
  ambiguity: [clear,ambiguous,underspecified]
oversample:
  - condition: "ambiguity==ambiguous or length>256"
    multiplier: 2
neg_controls:
  - typo_mutations: 200
  - nonsense: 200
  - instructionless: 200
```
raj: couple of metric notes: use exact-match where applicable, but prioritize semantic similarity (BERTScore / embedding cosine) + calibrated human judgments for subtle regressions. report mean delta and distribution tails (95th pct).

olivia: also report token-level latency and variance per-strata. quant schemes can have similar mean latency but different tail behavior which matters for SLAs.
kai: for AWQ/GPTQ we should run cross-checks with KV-cache stress test: repeated long conversational sequences to surface cache/kv quant errors. include 100 sessions of 50 turns.
emma: good call. we'll add conv_stress to probes.

eval-bot: run results posted: AWQ-int8 (mixed) vs GPTQ: initial pass on validation (10k) => AWQ: avg em_delta -1.8%, semantic delta -0.6%, tails (-95th) -4.2%. GPTQ: em_delta -2.4%, semantic -0.9%, tails -5.0%. latency: AWQ +12% vs FP16 baseline, GPTQ +8%. full logs -> link: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/quant-bakeoff/1854123456
emma: thanks bot. team: action items: (1) review sampling config in PR #412, (2) pick 1.2k human annotators for golden set checks, (3) schedule conv_stress runs on dedicated pool (raj), (4) freeze seed + pipeline code for reproducibility.
raj: i'll take conv_stress and seed freeze.
olivia: i'll own the human labeling plan and template guidelines.
kai: i'll finalize probe generation scripts and ensure mutation operators are deterministic.
emma: let's regroup after first overnight run. aim for a short postmortem with numbers + recommended deployment profile (safe: use AWQ?GPTQ hybrid fallback?)

emma: one last note — include a simple README snippet for SRE: how to interpret tail/regression alarms (example thresholds + rollback steps).
raj: can add. :white_check_mark:

emma: cool — thanks everyone :rocket:
